register.name: Green Energy Incentive Scheme
register.detail: Government of Seychelles · 2026 budget · Budget Speech of 12 February 2026
register.note: For households and small businesses installing grid-connected rooftop solar
register.text: A government scheme in the 2026 budget to help households and small businesses install grid-connected rooftop solar systems. It serves the energy standard and the Clean Grid, in a country where imported fossil fuels supply over 95% of electricity.
by: Ministry of Finance, Economic Planning, Trade and Investment

register.name: Affordable houses and apartments for professionals, 2026
register.detail: Government of Seychelles · 2026 budget · Budget Speech of 12 February 2026 · more than 200 affordable houses and over 120 apartments for professionals
register.note: The housing and land portfolio receives SR 854 million in 2026, 7.2% of the appropriation bill
register.text: The Government’s 2026 budget allocation to deliver more than 200 affordable houses and over 120 apartments for professionals. It serves the shelter standard, the furthest from reach in Seychelles.
by: Ministry of Finance, Economic Planning, Trade and Investment

register.name: Agriculture Development Fund
register.detail: Development Bank of Seychelles · 2026 budget · SR 76 million available at DBS, with an additional SR 30 million in the 2026 budget
register.note: A revised ADF agreement is to simplify and accelerate loan applications
register.text: Credit for farmers through the Agriculture Development Fund, available at the Development Bank of Seychelles, with resources for 2026 raised to SR 106 million. It serves the food and livelihood standards in an economy that imports much of its food.

register.name: Sovereign Blue Bond
register.detail: Republic of Seychelles · launched 2018 · backed by a $5M World Bank guarantee · a $5M concessional loan from the GEF partly covered its interest payments
register.note: The world’s first sovereign blue bond; SeyCCAT manages its blue grants and the Development Bank of Seychelles its blue loans
register.text: The world’s first sovereign blue bond, which raised $15 million from international investors for sustainable marine investments in the blue economy, through blue grants and blue loans. Its blue loans through the Development Bank of Seychelles serve the livelihood standard; issued in 2018, it is listed as an older instrument, and its term is not stated in the sources read.

register.name: Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.detail: IMF · approved 31 May 2023 · 36 months · EFF of SDR 42.365M (185% of quota) and RSF of SDR 34.350M (150% of quota) · fifth and sixth reviews completed 26 May 2026
register.note: The final reviews released about US$41 million; Directors welcomed the completion of both arrangements
register.text: IMF arrangements that supported Seychelles through successive shocks over three years: the EFF for macroeconomic stability and the RSF for climate resilience, including a reform measure to scale up renewable energy. The IMF notes that Seychelles imports about 95 percent of its energy, which ties the energy standard to that reform.

register.name: Second Sustainable and Inclusive Growth Development Policy Operation
register.detail: World Bank · IBRD · announced 6 May 2026 · second of a series that totals $45M
register.note: Benefit levels rose across six social protection programmes under the first operation of the series
register.text: A World Bank loan for reforms that expand private sector participation in renewable energy, strengthen financial sector supervision and cybercrime safeguards, improve the efficiency and transparency of public spending, reinforce climate action through improved waste management and support vulnerable youth. It serves the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Renewable Energy Acceleration Program
register.detail: World Bank · approved by the Board 30 May 2025 · first phase: $12.5M from the Green Climate Fund and $8M IBRD co-financing · Public Utilities Corporation
register.note: Renewables gave 5% of electricity in 2023; the national target is 15% by 2030
register.text: A World Bank programme to scale up renewable energy through grid modernisation, regulatory reform and technical assistance, and to unlock private investment, in a power system where imported fossil fuels supply over 95% of electricity. It serves the energy standard and the Clean Grid.

register.name: First Sustainable and Inclusive Growth Development Policy Operation
register.detail: World Bank · approved by the Board 27 November 2024 · the first of two planned operations
register.note: Benefit levels rose across six social protection programmes under this operation
register.text: A World Bank loan backing reforms for renewable energy, waste management, better social protection and opportunities for youth. It serves the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Solid Waste Management Project
register.note: Listed in the World Bank’s Seychelles portfolio
register.text: A World Bank project for waste services on the main islands.

register.name: Third Fiscal Sustainability and Climate Resilience DPF
register.detail: IBRD · Approved 11 January 2024 · the third of a series that totals $75M
register.note: Followed by the Sustainable and Inclusive Growth series from November 2024
register.text: Budget support for fiscal and climate reforms, to strengthen medium-term fiscal sustainability, build resilience and strengthen policies for inclusive and sustainable growth.

register.name: Economic Resilience and Green Recovery Support Programme, third phase (ERGRSP-III)
register.detail: African Development Bank · approved 22 September 2026 · third and final phase · follows phases of $25M each in 2024 and 2025
register.note: Brings the Bank Group’s total financing across the three phases to $84 million
register.text: A loan for reforms in economic governance and public financial management, the business environment and climate resilience, which also advances employment and skills reforms. The series began with a first phase aimed at improving access to renewable energy and creating jobs, and serves the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: 81 housing units at Barbarons
register.detail: Abu Dhabi Fund for Development · funding secured, as announced in the Budget Speech of 12 February 2026 · SR 75 million allocated to the project in the 2026 budget
register.note: The amount of the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development financing is not stated
register.text: Funding from the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development for the construction of 81 housing units at Barbarons. It serves the shelter standard, the furthest from reach in Seychelles.

register.name: 72 housing units at Beoliere
register.detail: Government of China · Budget Speech of 12 February 2026 · SR 102 million for 72 units at Beoliere through Chinese Government funding
register.note: The same passage gives SR 102 million for 64 units at Cap Bonm Zan; it does not say whether the Chinese funding covers them too
register.text: Housing at Beoliere built through funding from the Government of China, within the Government’s 2026 housing programme. It serves the shelter standard, the furthest from reach in Seychelles.

register.name: Special Economic Package
register.detail: Government of India · Joint Vision of 9 February 2026 · $125M rupee-denominated line of credit and $50M in grant assistance
register.note: India also agreed to work with Seychelles on a new hospital; the Joint Vision records donations of 1,000 tonnes of grains and 10 ambulances
register.text: A package of a line of credit and grants for development cooperation projects, announced in the India–Seychelles Joint Vision for Sustainability, Economic Growth and Security through Enhanced Linkages. The two governments will work together to support the construction of a new hospital, which serves the health standard; the release does not list the projects the package will finance.

register.name: Seysun Lagoon floating solar plant, Qair
register.detail: Facility for Energy Inclusion, managed by Cygnum Capital · senior debt announced 20 August 2025 · 5.8 MWp in the Providence Lagoon on Mahé · 25-year power purchase agreement with the Public Utilities Corporation
register.note: Described by its lender as the first utility-scale independent power project in Seychelles
register.text: Senior debt for a floating solar plant that Qair is developing on Mahé, which will sell its power to the Public Utilities Corporation for 25 years. It serves the energy standard and the Clean Grid, as the first private utility-scale solar plant in a grid that runs almost entirely on imported fuel.
